entities.name: Therac-25
entities.why: The Therac-25 is the faulty machine that is the subject of the entire story and responsible for all the incidents.

entities.name: Software (Code / Bugs)
entities.why: The inherent flaws in the software, and the overconfidence in it, are the core of the story's problem.

entities.name: Radiation (Overdose / Dose)
entities.why: The uncontrolled radiation output is the direct mechanism of harm and the central threat.

entities.name: Beam
entities.why: The uncontrolled firing of the electron or X-ray beam was the immediate cause of physical harm to patients.

entities.name: AECL
entities.why: As the manufacturer, AECL made critical design decisions and initially denied responsibility for the accidents.

entities.name: Katherine Yarbrough
entities.why: She is the first patient whose suffering initiates the narrative and illustrates the machine's failure.

entities.name: Control Terminal (Console / Screen)
entities.why: It is the human-machine interface where errors were introduced and false assurances given.

entities.name: Hardware (Safety Interlocks / Fuses)
entities.why: The deliberate removal of redundant hardware interlocks allowed the software bugs to become lethal.

entities.name: Operator (Tyler)
entities.why: Her fast typing was the trigger for the race condition, and her collaboration with Fritz Hager exposed the bug.

entities.name: Target (Metal)
entities.why: Its incorrect positioning, due to software errors, was the immediate physical cause of overdose in X-ray mode.

entities.name: Arithmetic Overflow (Single Byte Counter)
entities.why: This specific software flaw bypassed safety checks due to an unexpected counter rollover.

entities.name: Fritz Hager
entities.why: He was instrumental in demonstrating and exposing the software bugs by reproducing the incidents.

entities.name: Race Condition
entities.why: This specific software flaw directly led to the machine firing at full power without the target in place.

entities.name: Malfunction 54
entities.why: This specific error code was a critical, yet ignored, warning sign that pointed to the underlying malfunctions.

entities.name: Hospital (Setting)
entities.why: The hospital setting is where all the patient incidents took place, highlighting the tragic irony of a place of healing becoming one of harm.

entities.name: Tyler (East Texas Cancer Center)
entities.why: Tyler is the site of critical incidents and where the specific software bug was finally reproduced and identified.

entities.name: Voyne Ray Cox
entities.why: His case, along with Kidd's, was crucial in demonstrating the race condition bug triggered by operator speed.

entities.name: Yakima
entities.why: Yakima is the site of multiple, recurring incidents, demonstrating the widespread and unaddressed nature of the problem.

entities.name: Verdon Kidd
entities.why: His death spurred the hospital physicist, Fritz Hager, to investigate and reproduce the error.

entities.name: Glen Dodd
entities.why: His death demonstrated the return of the specific arithmetic overflow bug in a previously affected location.

entities.name: FDA
entities.why: The FDA's intervention ultimately led to the declaration of the Therac-25 as defective and its eventual removal.

entities.name: Frances Hill
entities.why: She is documented as the first fatality attributed to the Therac-25's malfunction.

entities.name: Nancy Leveson
entities.why: Her definitive investigation became a standard case study, providing crucial understanding of the accidents.

entities.name: Clark Turner
entities.why: He co-authored the definitive investigation into the Therac-25 accidents.

entities.name: Older Therac Models (Therac-6, Therac-20)
entities.why: They provide crucial context for the Therac-25's design choices and the history of its embedded software bugs.

entities.name: Nineteen Eighty-Five
entities.why: It establishes the historical context for the start of the incidents and the technology involved.

entities.name: Tim Still
entities.why: He was the first to suspect the machine and question AECL, even if his concerns were initially dismissed.

entities.name: Single Programmer
entities.why: The fact that a single programmer wrote the critical safety software highlights the resource constraints and potential for error.
